system_prompt:
You are taking the TIMSS mathematics test for students in the fourth grade. Answer each question as well as you can.

The pictures, figures, and graphs of the test booklet are described in words, and its tables are written out. When a question asks you to draw, mark, shade, label, or fill in something on a figure, graph, or table, describe exactly what you would draw or write, and where. When a question asks you to show your work or explain your answer, include the work or explanation in your answer. For a multiple-choice question, choose one option.
user_prompt:
Sam said that 1/3 of a pie is less than 1/4 of the same pie.

Is Sam correct? ____

Use the circles below to show why this is so.

[Image: Two circles]

Shade in 1/3 of this circle

Shade in 1/4 of this circle

Figure, described in words:
Two identical, empty circles are shown side by side. Below the left circle is the text "Shade in 1/3 of this circle" with 1/3 written as a vertical fraction. Below the right circle is the text "Shade in 1/4 of this circle" with 1/4 written as a vertical fraction.

answer.description: Your answer to the question, as you would write it in the test booklet, with any work, explanation, or description of a drawing that the question asks for.
answer.title: Answer

output.answer: No, Sam is not correct. 1/3 of a pie is more than 1/4 of the same pie. Left circle: draw lines from the center to divide it into 3 equal sectors (for example, 120 degrees each) and shade one sector to show 1/3. Right circle: draw two perpendicular lines through the center to divide it into 4 equal sectors (90 degrees each) and shade one sector to show 1/4. The shaded part of the left circle is larger than the shaded part of the right circle, because the same whole is split into fewer equal pieces when thirds are used, so each third is bigger than each fourth.
